title: The Operational Facilitator reviews proposals for alignment with both the Sky Core Atlas and the Agent's own Artifact
content:
A.2.2.9.1.2.3.4.2 states the review standard: "The Operational Facilitator reviews the `Artifact Edit Proposal` to ensure alignment with **the Sky Core Atlas and the Agent Artifact**."

Two reference documents, not one. Ecosystem-level compliance is the obvious half. The second half means an Agent's own previously ratified rules — its Omni Documents, its Root Edit process requirements, its Instance parameters — are enforced against it by an external reviewer. An Agent cannot quietly contradict its own constitution by passing a later proposal that ignores it.

This is what gives Agent-level self-governance any durability. Under A.2.2.6.2.2.2 an Agent designs its own governance process; without external enforcement, those self-imposed constraints would bind only as long as the Agent found them convenient. Having the Facilitator — who also runs the vote and actions the edit — check proposals against the Artifact makes the Agent's own commitments effective against itself.

It also gives Agent token holders something real to rely on. A holder who accepted a quorum threshold, an eligible-proposer rule, or a parameter constraint is protected by a party structurally separate from the Agent's management, rather than by the Agent's continued goodwill.

The cost is that the Facilitator must be fluent in each Agent's bespoke Artifact as well as the Atlas, which is precisely why the Executor Accord ties a Prime Agent to a specific Operational Executor rather than to a generic reviewer pool.
description: An Agent's self-authored rules bind its later proposals: a proposal consistent with ecosystem-level rules can still be rejected for conflicting with the Agent's own Artifact.
